events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

args.content:
# My books

A small app for tracking what you're reading. No accounts, no database, no dependencies beyond Node 20+.

```sh
npm start        # http://127.0.0.1:3000
npm test
```

Books are saved to `data/books.json`, so they survive a restart.

Settings (environment variables):

| Variable      | Default            | Purpose                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PORT`        | `3000`             | Port to listen on                                              |
| `HOST`        | `127.0.0.1`        | Address to listen on. Use `0.0.0.0` to allow other machines in |
| `DATA_FILE`   | `data/books.json`  | Where books are saved                                          |
| `PUBLIC_URL`  | taken from request | Base URL for share links, e.g. `https://books.example.com`     |

events.content:
I've built the app as a plain Node server with no dependencies. Books are saved to `data/books.json`, so they're still there after a restart. The 10 tests pass, and I also started the real server, added a book through the form, and checked that it was written to the file and showed up on its own page.

**To run it:** `npm start`, then open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

**What it does:**
- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, with a form underneath to add a book (title, author, notes). Title is the only required field.
- **Mark finished:** a button next to each book you're reading, and another on the book's own page. It records the date you finished.
- **Book page:** shows the title, author, notes (line breaks kept) and whether you're reading it or when you finished it.
- **Sharing:** each book's page has its own address, like `/books/6wVzUQ_J`, and shows that full link ready to copy.

**Things to know about sharing:**
- **It only listens on your own computer by default.** A link like `http://127.0.0.1:3000/...` won't work for anyone else. For someone else to open it, the app has to run somewhere they can reach. You can make it accept connections from other machines with `HOST=0.0.0.0`. If it's behind a proper web address, set `PUBLIC_URL=https://your-address` so the share links use that address.
- **Without accounts, anyone who can reach the app has full access.** Someone you send a link to could go to the home page, see all your books, add new ones, or mark one finished. That's the trade-off of skipping accounts. If it matters, the simplest fix is to make the book page read-only for visitors and protect everything else with one password. I haven't done that because you asked for nothing fancy.

**How the data is protected:** the file is saved in a way that a crash halfway through can't leave it half-written. If the file ever becomes unreadable, the app refuses to start rather than replacing it with an empty list.

There's no way to edit notes after you've added a book yet, since you didn't ask for it, but it would be easy to add. The main code is in `src/app.js`, `src/views.js` and `src/store.js`, with `server.js` to start it and a short README listing the settings. I haven't committed anything.
